qt: to the Commission Galato Alexandraki (ECR) Subject:

The 2025 Environmental Implementation Review found that Greece was experiencing serious delays in urban wastewater projects, a continued reliance on waste landfilling and systemic failures in complying with EU Court of Justice rulings. The overall environmental investment gap is estimated at EUR 2.3 billion a year. The report warns that the overcapacity of residual waste treatment facilities is not helping Greece’s transition to the circular economy. Resources need to go into infrastructure that works and meets the country’s needs. Clear answers need to be given regarding the delayed projects. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What corrective measures and timelines have been agreed with the Greek authorities for the most major outstanding waste and urban waste water issues identified in the report?
Which EU-funded projects relating to waste and wastewater are experiencing delays, and what is the funding, implementation stage and expected date of entry into operation for each of these projects?
How does it check that Greek investments meet actual needs and cover separate collection, without creating oversized residual waste facilities?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) The 2025 Environmental Implementation Review for Greece1 identifies waste management performance and urban wastewater treatment capacity as two of the most critical environmental issues for which recommendations have been delivered. In both cases, the Commission continues to compel Greece to comply with legal requirements and collects the fines imposed by rulings of the Court of Justice of the EU. It is up to Member States to choose the most effective ways to implement EU laws and policies, as long as they achieve the EU’s common environmental objectives and targets laid down therein. Under Cohesion Policy 2021-20272, around EUR 626 million is allocated to wastewater investments in Greece3. Approved projects, including wastewater treatment plants, sewage networks and private connections, amount to EUR 946 million (151% of the allocation), with EUR 213 million in payments (34%)4. In addition, EUR 675 million is allocated to waste management investments in Greece, but implementation remains limited (7% selected, 0.3% payments). A EUR 480 million call under the Environment and Climate Change programme is open until April 20275. As the enabling condition on updated waste management plans6 is currently considered unfulfilled, related expenditure cannot yet be reimbursed by the Commission. Detailed project-level information can be sought from the competent Greek authorities7. For the 2021-2027 period, Greece has adopted a new waste management model based on facilities8 that process separately collected waste, with a gradually declining input of mixed waste. The financing model agreed for these facilities links funding to separate collection and recycling performance, helping incentivise recycling and avoid overcapacity.
